notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, labeled FY2026 as in the Toyota record (the 20-F uses only 'fiscal year ended March 31, 2026'; matches data.js fy 'Mar 2026'). Source: Form 20-F filed June 18, 2026 (accession 0001193125-26-274893) on www.sec.gov; IFRS, figures in billions of yen (JPY), no FX conversion. SEC companyfacts has no facts for this year, so no xbrl objects are recorded. FINANCIAL SERVICES: Sony executed the Partial Spin-off of its Financial Services business (Sony Financial Group, SFGI) during the year; it is now a discontinued operation and was deconsolidated, and prior years are restated, so sales and the geography table are continuing operations only. The SFGI shares Sony distributed to its shareholders were a dividend in kind, not cash, and are not in the cash dividends figure (the 20-F says its dividend figures 'do not include dividends in kind of the shares of SFGI'). AKIO MORITA is deceased. The 20-F names no Morita family member, estate or foundation among major shareholders, so family is null. MAJOR SHAREHOLDERS: the 20-F lists Bulk Shareholding Reports above 5% filed with the Kanto Local Finance Bureau; percentages are as stated in each report (on the issued share capital at that time), asOf is each report date, and the reports do not say whether holdings are direct or beneficial. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line 'Dividends paid' (¥135,028m). BUYBACKS: 'Payments for purchases of treasury stock' (¥522,089m); the 20-F says Sony completed ¥500.0 billion of repurchases from May 15, 2025 to March 24, 2026. STOCK COMP: ¥39,102m, which the 20-F says includes expenses of the Financial Services business.

footprint.notes: Sony's FY2025 20-F (year ended March 31, 2026) splits employees only into Japan (42,300) and outside Japan (52,600), with no country detail; the total fell to about 94,900 from 112,300 mainly because Sony Financial Group was deconsolidated after the partial spin-off of the Financial Services business, plus ET&S restructuring in Japan and I&SS divestitures outside Japan. Item 4.D lists major facilities as of March 31, 2026 with carrying amounts and employee counts, and the sites come from that table (all twelve sites listed last year are still in it). The last number in each site quote is the employee count; subsidiary counts are rounded to the nearest hundred and, for entities marked *5, include their subsidiaries. Sony Corporation of America's row spans three segment lines (1,500, 6,700 and 1,500 employees), and only the first line is quoted. A separate corporate 'Others' row (primarily Sony City Osaki and Atsugi TEC, per the filing's footnote) is not listed as a site. Sony Pictures' 'primary location' is given as Delaware in the filing, although its studio operations are not described there. No state-level or tax-by-country data was found in the 20-F.

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (FY2026 Form 20-F). The Financial Services business was partially spun off and is presented as a discontinued operation, so revenue, operating cash flow and capex are all on the continuing-operations basis (operating cash flow including discontinued operations was 1,945,617, with discontinued −20,675). The insurance and bank flows that sat inside the old operating cash flow are therefore gone, and financeReceivablesInOCF is now false. IFRS filer that classifies interest and dividends paid and received in operating activities (stated in the 20-F), and income taxes in operating, so nothing is added back. Capex is one combined line for PP&E and other intangible assets; purchases of businesses (185,355) excluded. Content-asset spending (665,894) is inside operating cash flow and so counts as paid out. No xbrl objects: companyfacts has no facts for this fiscal year. FX: fiscal year ends March 2026; the calendar-2025 average covers 9 of its 12 months.

Shares = 5,965,316,326 issued − 136,679,029 treasury = 5,828,637,297 at October 31, 2026, from Sony's monthly share-repurchase status report filed on Form 6-K on November 12, 2026, which states both parts but not the difference.
